## Abstract

Kate Kitagawa’s journey through mathematics is marked by a unique blend of storytelling, global curiosity, and an inclusive perspective on history. Her book, The Secret Lives of Numbers, co-authored with Timothy Revell, exemplifies her approach to mathematics as an ever-evolving, interconnected story that transcends borders, gender, and time. This work explores mathematics from early tally marks to the complexity of quantum physics, celebrating unsung figures whose contributions have been overlooked due to historical biases. The book’s focus on global perspectives challenges traditional Eurocentric narratives, showcasing mathematics as a collaborative “international team sport”.
